2. Opposite party No.1 of this Civil Revision petition in the capacity of a co-sharer by inheritance as pre-emptor impleading petitioner as pre-emptee laid a case being Miscellaneous case No.6 of 1986 in the Fourth Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge Narayanganj under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for an order of pre-emption with respect to land described in schedule to Miscellaneous case. The said Miscellaneous case was renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 18 of 1990 on transfer to second Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Narayanganj Pre-emptee-petitioner was a stranger to the case holding. 

 12. In approaching the said question provision contained in section 117 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act may conveniently be noticed. Section 117 (1)( c) enshrines that for the purpose of sub-division of a joint tenancy for distribution of rent and for effecting a sub-division of a joint tenancy an application is required to be filed and notice is required to be given to all the parties concerned to appear and be heard in the matter and notice having not been served upon co-sharers, mutation and sub-division effected behind their back cannot said to be valid sub-division or splitting up of jama and in such case co-sharer in the joint tenancy cannot be said to have lost their right of pre-emption. 

 13. Pre-emptee-petitioner claimed that joint tenancy had been sub-divided and new jama had been created in the name of the seller and also in the name of pre-emptee-petitioner. This contention of the pre-emptee-petitioner has been negatived by pre-emptor-opposite party raising contention that joint tenancy or holding was not sub-divided and she did not cease to be a co-sharer in holding and the pre-emptee-petitioner remains to be a stranger to case holding. 

 14. Exhibit-ka and ka(1) are mutated khatians in the name of Golam Mustafa Bhuiyan, seller opposite party No. 2 and Exhibit-kha (1) is a Rent Receipt manifesting payment of rent by pre-emptee petitioner and Exhibit-kha (2) is a niutated Khatian in the name of pre-emptee-petitioner, Except those documents no other documents had been produced from the side of pre-emptee-petitioner evidencing that for sub-division of the joint tenancy application was filed before Revenue Officer and notices upon co-sharers had been issued and co-sharers had been heard in the alleged sub-division matter. In the absence of those it cannot be at all suggested that the joint tenancy had been sub-divided and a separate Jama and tenancy had been created in the name of seller opposite party and pre-emptee-petitioner. There cannot be any sub-division of holding and splitting up of Jama unless requirements of law embodied in section 117 (1) (c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act have been complied with.
